newsitem.title: USA: SITEL DROPS ON DOWNGRADES, EARNINGS OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: SITEL DROPS ON DOWNGRADES, EARNINGS OUTLOOK.

text.p: Shares of SITEL Corp lost about 28 percent after several brokerage firms downgraded the stock, citing a lack of "upside surprise" in its second quarter earnings and potential weakness in margins in the second half of the year.
SITEL, which provides outsourced telephone-based customer service and sales programs, lost 4-1/8 to 11-1/8 in midday trading.
SITEL posted second quarter operation earnings of $0.10 a share compared with $0.06 a share on an 81 percent increase in revenues.
SITEL's results met the Wall Street consensus, but higher interest expenses and higher taxes prevented an upside suprise in earnings, analysts said.
SITEl is expected to face near-term earnings volatility, analysts said.

"Sales growth is expected to remain strong in the second half of 1997 and 1998....however, the company is spending aggressively to fuel big gains in 1998 and this will compromise second half margins," said Dillon Read analyst Thomas O'Halloran in a research report.
Dillon Read downgraded SITEL and trimmed its 1997 earnings estimate to $0.38 a share from $0.45 a share and cut the 1998 estimate to $0.58 a share from $0.63 a share.
Alex. Brown also downgraded the stock.
